lines.en: What empathy requires is not that we feel the same pain, but that we believe it is real.
It is often the person who laughs the loudest who carries the heaviest heart.
Were we to judge every action by its hidden grief, most anger would look like a call for help.
However hard we try to hide them, our feelings leak out in a hundred small ways every day.
Not until someone has sat with us in silence, without advice, do we feel truly heard.
It is said that courage is not the absence of fear, but the decision that something else matters more.
What children sense instantly, adults often spend years relearning: that feelings are facts of their own kind.
The apology, though only two words long, took him three years to say.
Little do we know of the storms inside the people we pass every day.
Rarely does advice comfort the grieving; presence comforts them far more than words.
What grief needs from us is not solutions but the patience to simply remain in the room.
It is a rare skill to hear anger and answer the fear that hides beneath it.
Were we to rank emotions by honesty, the ones we hide would top the list.
Not until we forgive ourselves do most of us find the strength to apologize to others.
However rational we believe ourselves to be, our decisions are made of feeling long before reason arrives.
